attribution.note: Marcus wrote these words himself in his own Substack post, in his own voice.

semantics.note: The drafter's version keeps 'currently', 'almost no' and the narrower scope of Musk's contemplated robots. It is a firm present-tense description, so it is an observation.

contract.note: The plain reading (meaningful binding constraints nearly absent) is fair and ordinary. Counting general laws as well as AI-specific rules leans a little against him, since 'regulation around AI' usually means AI-specific rules. The open jurisdiction and the lack of any coverage threshold make interpretation decisive.

evidence.note: A CRS report dated June 2025. It says there is no broad federal AI law but notes targeted provisions, existing agency authorities and new state laws. It does not measure total coverage on July 15.

A Commission notice that the first EU AI Act rules (literacy and a very limited set of prohibitions) applied from February 2025. It shows some binding rules existed but not how broad they were. It says nothing about robots.

reviews.rationale: Both items show some binding AI rules existed (targeted US provisions, state laws, limited EU prohibitions), and also that there was no broad US federal framework. 'Almost no' allows for some rules, so neither item settles whether coverage was negligible or substantial. The packet itself admits it lacks a complete review and found no accessible evidence on robotics rules, so the outcome is unresolved.
